fixtures.title: How does your memory work? (University of the Netherlands), 3:35 excerpt
fixtures.author: Universiteit van Nederland (University of the Netherlands); speaker Dr. Lisa Genzel, Radboud University
fixtures.attribution: "How does your memory work" by Universiteit van Nederland (speaker: Dr. Lisa Genzel, Radboud University), CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Trimmed to 43.447 s + 215.2 s and transcoded to H.264/AAC MP4 for the WeftCut bench; the derivative is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.
fixtures.notes: English lecture from a virtual studio set: one speaker (Lisa Genzel) on camera, cutting between wide shots, a medium close-up to camera and shots of her beside a large slide screen (brain diagrams with labels, then photo/illustration slides). Not a literal screen recording, but long stretches are slide-led. Source window starts on a scene cut and keyframe at source 43.447 s, right at 'let's start at the very beginning: what is a memory', which skips the channel intro and the burned-in name lower third at source ~30 s, so the excerpt carries no on-screen name. Excerpt times (approximate, from the YouTube auto-captions on Commons, +/- 1 s): 0-3 wide establishing shot, speech from ~2.5; 3-22 medium close-up to camera; 22-64 neurons and networks (slide: brain network); ~64-131 first memory hub, the hippocampus ('the first hub is the hippocampus' ~71.5; patient example ~90-121); ~131-176 second hub, the cortex ('this is the second memory hub, the cortex' ~131); ~176-214.7 example of a city walk becoming a spatial map in the cortex, slide of a street photo and a route map. Speech ends at ~214.7; the last ~0.7 s is the next shot (wide), cut at 214.52. Pauses (silencedetect -34 dB, >= 0.4 s): about 60, mostly 0.5-2.0 s between sentences, e.g. 3.8-4.9, 11.6-12.8, 22.1-23.6, 40.1-41.8, 56.7-58.6, 69.7-71.7, 105.2-106.7, 165.3-167.2. The bench file is an H.264/AAC MP4 transcoded from the stream-copy trim (see transcode); ffmpeg may print one 'Error parsing Opus packet header' warning, which is in the source and decodes fine.
